scope: verifier-side only; never injected into the agent environment

programmatic.description: The authoritative samples verify, round-trip byte for byte, and expose the documented segment sequence.
programmatic.pass_condition: verify() accepts both assets/sample.wlsg and assets/sample_empty.wlsg; pack(unpack(sample)) reproduces the sample byte for byte; unpack(sample) yields exactly the (seg_id, payload) sequence the samples encode, in file order; the zero-segment sample round-trips too.
programmatic.failure_reason: The implementation rejects or misreads the authoritative samples, or re-packing a parsed sample produces different bytes (which breaks downstream byte-hash incremental sync).

programmatic.description: Segments follow the on-disk layout of the real samples: fixed-width little-endian fields, every segment padded to an 8-byte boundary, and an 8-byte (offset, length) entry per segment in the tail index.
programmatic.pass_condition: Every segment starts on an 8-byte boundary and the declared entry length covers the stored padding, so byte offsets match the authoritative samples exactly; the tail index carries both the offset and the length of each segment and is laid out exactly as the sample is.
programmatic.failure_reason: Segment encoding or padding does not match the byte layout of the authoritative samples, or the index entries omit a field so offsets drift even though self-generated containers still round-trip.

programmatic.description: The trailer is a general CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over the header plus the whole segment region and over the index region: it matches the standard check vectors and catches tampering anywhere in either covered region.
programmatic.pass_condition: compute_crc() matches a published standard check value for a known test vector; verify() returns False once segment content, segment padding or index bytes are altered; the segment-region digest covers the header, every segment header, every payload and the alignment padding.
programmatic.failure_reason: The checksum is a private or truncated fold that agrees with the sample only by accident, is computed over a subset of the container (for example skipping the header or the padding), or silently accepts tampered content.

programmatic.description: Structural and integrity problems raise WSegError with the documented kind, insufficient data is always classified as truncated before any contradiction is considered, and verify() never raises.
programmatic.pass_condition: A container that ends before the structure it declares can be read raises kind 'truncated' on the batch and the streaming path alike, including a wholly missing index region, a partly missing index, a missing trailer and a segment header that declares more payload than the file holds; a container whose bytes are all present but contradict each other raises kind 'structure', including an index offset that points inside the header, a segment that runs past the index region, index entries that disagree with the derived segment layout, a segment count that disagrees with the index region size, and bytes trailing the trailer; a wrong magic raises kind 'magic'; an unsupported version raises kind 'version'; verify() returns False for every malformed input instead of propagating ValueError, struct.error or IndexError.
programmatic.failure_reason: Malformed input leaks a built-in exception, the error kind does not distinguish the documented categories, insufficient data is reported as 'structure' (or accepted as valid), a structural contradiction is reported as 'checksum', or verify() raises instead of returning False.

programmatic.description: iter_segments() is lazy: it only issues fixed-size read(n) calls and yields the first segment after reading a small prefix of the container.
programmatic.pass_condition: iter_segments() never issues an unbounded read (no read(), read(-1) or readlines()); the first segment is yielded after consuming only a bounded prefix of the stream, and the trailer is still verified after the last segment.
programmatic.failure_reason: The iterator buffers the whole container before yielding, so a few-hundred-MB container is still pulled into memory as one object.

programmatic.description: The public surface stays intact and self-consistent: small / empty-payload / generated containers round-trip, pack() rejects invalid input, and read_all() matches unpack().
programmatic.pass_condition: pack/unpack round-trips for small segments, empty payloads and freshly generated containers; pack() output is accepted by both verify() and iter_segments(); read_all() returns the same segments as unpack(); pack() raises WSegError for an out-of-range segment id and for a non-bytes payload.
programmatic.failure_reason: Regression in the public API or in self-produced containers: round-trip only works for the sample shape, read_all() disagrees with unpack(), or invalid input is silently accepted.
